jobs.occupation: Key Account Manager
jobs.description:
KEY
ACCOUNT MANAGER 

Vald.
BIRN A/S in Holstebro is looking for a technically qualified and commercially
focused Key Account Manager for its sales of high quality cast iron solutions.

THE
POSITION

In order
to consolidate and expand our sales activities, we need to strengthen our sales
team by recruiting a qualified Key Account Manager.

You will
be given responsibility for strategically important customers, all of which are
market-leading OEMs or system providers, including those in the truck sector.
Your role will be to expand and enhance the sales turnover among existing
customers, while at the same time cultivating new customer relationships. A
significant part of the role also involves making sustained efforts to secure
up-to-date framework agreements and contracts in addition to communicating
customer requirements and expectations.

The sales
process consists of offering to produce the customers’ cast iron components.
Once the items are being produced, the sales work will involve continuously
negotiating and adjusting the sales prices of the individual components, as
well as negotiating and maintaining other commercial conditions. These
conditions include packaging, logistics solutions, framework agreements for
quality and delivery, and aftermarket terms. 

Your
normal working day will vary from administrative tasks at the office in
Holstebro, where you will work closely with Production, the Production
Engineering Department (PED), Business Controlling and other company
stakeholders. You will also be responsible for planning and conducting your
external customer visits, primarily in Europe where you can expect up to around
50 days’ travelling per year. You will also help with and prepare data and
presentations for sales meetings and trade fair attendance, as well as
continuously reporting to Sales Management. 

As part
of a cross-organisational partnership, you will familiarise yourself with the
customers’ projects and thus become the most important link of the contact
between the customer and your colleagues across the entire organisation.

When out
visiting customers with a view to sales, you will always have a ‘One Stop Shop’
cast iron solution to call upon. By this, we mean that BIRN is able to cast, machine,
assemble and surface-treat the products so that they can be delivered directly
to the customer’s production line or application without further processing.
This is both efficient and sustainable.

Are you
looking to combine your technical curiosity and skills with a strategic
responsibility for sales and long-term customer relationships in an
international industrial group? If so, you may be the person we are looking for
as a Key Account Manager. 

YOUR
DUTIES

You will
be given a central role in the sales organisation, with your work including the
following:

• Responsibility
for and the continued development of a portfolio of four to six major strategic
customers in Europe, primarily in Scandinavia. You will be responsible for a
turnover of at least € 25 million
• Building
up long-term relationships with the customers’ stakeholders in the fields of
purchasing, development, quality and logistics
• Technical
and commercial advice during the customers’ development and project phases
• Planning
and conducting customer visits, contract and price negotiations and major
framework agreements
• Ongoing
budget monitoring, forecasts and sales reports at customer level
• Searching
for, analysing and developing new customer potentials and market segments
• Close
internal collaboration with production engineering, quality, controlling and
finance
• Participation
in sales and strategy activities across the organisation
The
position involves some travel, primarily in Europe.

QUALIFICATIONS

We expect
you to have the following:

• Extensive
advanced technical training/experience, ideally supplemented with commercial
skills, e.g. engineer, marine engineer or equivalent. A skilled trade
background, supplemented by commercial training or experience, is another
option
• Experience
of technical sales, project sales or Key Account Management; alternatively, you
will have been recently trained and have the right level of drive. The start
date will be adapted to suit the right candidate
• The
ability to thrive in an outward-facing role with extensive customer contact,
and to plan your day-to-day work independently
• The
ability to work in a structured manner on CRM, budgets, documentation and
monitoring. You will need to be skilled in using digital tools, for processing
both text and numbers
• The
ability to communicate without difficulty in English and, preferably, also in
Danish – and, ideally, in the other Scandinavian languages
• The
technical flair and ability to get to grips with the customers’ business and
applications
• A
passenger car driving licence and a valid passport with no travel restrictions
At a
personal level, you will be skilled in relationships, persistent and curious,
with the motivation to create value through collaboration based on trust and a
high level of professionalism.

WHAT WE
OFFER

You will
become part of Vald. BIRN A/S, a solid and internationally represented
industrial enterprise with strong values and a high degree of professionalism.
In addition, you will receive:

• A
central, independent role with a high level of influence on customers, sales
and commercial development
• A strong
professional environment with close collaboration across the Group
• Thorough
on-boarding and training in products, markets and the organisation
• Good
opportunities for both professional and personal development
• Attractive
terms and conditions of employment, including a pension scheme and health
insurance
• A good
canteen scheme and active staff association
• An
informal work environment that focuses on well-being, responsibility and
sustainability
ABOUT THE
BIRN GROUP

Vald.
BIRN A/S in Holstebro is the Group Headquarters of one of Northern Europe’s
largest foundry Groups. We supply highly processed cast iron components to the truck
industry and others, as well as industrial hydraulics and machine components.
Sustainability, the circular economy and responsibility are integral parts of
our DNA. The Group employs around 750 staff, of which around 480 are
in Holstebro.

APPLICATIONS

If you
have any questions about the position or the BIRN Group, please feel free to
contact Group CSO Peter Frost Jepsen on tel. +45 3016 0160 or Group
HR Manager Morten Madsen on tel. +45 3016 0115.

Please
note that we are processing applications on a continuous basis and will close
the position once we have found the right candidate. As mentioned above, the
start date can be adjusted to suit the right candidate. Please submit your
application via our recruitment system, which you will find at [insert link].
Candidates who proceed to a second interview can expect to complete a
personality profile as part of the process.

We would
encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, ethnicity or age, to
apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance - Functional Solution Architect
jobs.description:
Are you a Functional Solution Architect with a passion for providing top-notch service to customers, focusing on quality when implementing D365 solutions?

Join our team at TravelOperations and help us design and implement cutting-edge solutions that meet our clients' complex business needs.

Responsibilities

As a Functional Solution Architect at TravelOperations, you will play a key role in influencing and overseeing large-scale international implementation projects.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Design and implement enterprise-level solutions, ensuring they align with business objectives and technical requirements.

• 
Collaborate with stakeholders to define functional requirements and develop architecture roadmaps.

• 
Lead the integration of multiple systems to create seamless business processes.

• 
Ensure solutions are scalable, secure, and compliant with industry standards.

• 
Provide technical leadership and mentor team members in best practices and emerging technologies.

• 
Execute workshops, including in-depth analysis sessions, in collaboration with a team of Business Consultants to refine and validate solution designs.

• 
Collaborate with skilled Developers to ensure the solution design is thoroughly tested and meets the technical and functional requirements.

• 
Engage in General Architect work, such as exploring emerging technologies, conducting Proof of Concepts, and participating in Product Advisory Board activities with partners like Microsoft or industry-specific leaders such as Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport.

• 
Offer internal guidance and support to colleagues, fostering a culture of knowledge sharing and continuous improvement in architectural best practices.

• 
Maintaining daily ownership of customer relationships, acting as a trusted advisor in implementing scalable and secure solutions.

Desired Skills & Requirements

Seeking a candidate with 5+ years of Dynamics 365 Finance experience with a strong finance background. While various profiles may apply, we highly value a strong person-organization fit. Our ideal candidate possesses the following attributes and qualifications:

• 
Extensive experience with Dynamics 365 Finance and proficiency in finance.

• 
Proven experience as a Functional Solution Architect or in a similar role.

• 
Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks and methodologies.

• 
Proficiency in system integration, data migration, and cloud technologies.

• 
Excellent communication skills to articulate complex solutions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• 
Ability to manage multiple projects and deliver high-quality solutions within tight deadlines and the capability to lead functional areas within projects.

• 
Certification in MB-310 / MB-700.

• 
Dynamic, proactive, and possesses a comprehensive solution overview.

• 
Exceptional consulting and communication skills in English, both written and verbal.

• 
Demonstrated passion for driving positive change for customers and their businesses, coupled with a willingness to travel both professionally and personally.

Why Join Us?

• 
Opportunity to work with innovative technologies in a dynamic environment where progressive work culture with a global perspective where your ideas truly matter, and growth opportunities are endless.

• 
Work with the latest Microsoft Technologies alongside Dynamics professionals committed to driving customer success.

• 
Enjoy the flexibility to work from anywhere

• 
Work-life balance that suits your lifestyle.

• 
Experience a dynamic workplace where team spirit, joy, and productivity go hand in hand.

• 
Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.

• 
Career growth and professional development opportunities.

• 
A collaborative and inclusive work culture.

Workplace

Work from either our Copenhagen or Aalborg offices and have the chance to visit our Brisbane location. Join our global team spanning Denmark, Sweden, India, the US, and Australia.

How to Apply

For more details, please contact our People and Culture Team at hr@traveloperations.com or

visit our careers site at www.traveloperations.com.

We can't wait to hear from you!

Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis.

About Travel Operations A/S

At TravelOperations, we're not just about professionalism and ambition; we're about building an environment where every employee shines. Our global reach spans from Greenland to Australia, as we partner with leading travel agencies, airlines, and leisure-focused businesses to craft tailor-made solutions. Join us in reshaping the travel industry landscape, where responsiveness and innovation are our guiding stars.

Diversity and Inclusion

At our company, Diversity and Inclusion are core values. We welcome applicants of all genders, striving for a workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. Join us in building an inclusive future where diversity is celebrated as a strength

jobs.description:
Are you an experienced Business Central professional who thrives on transforming businesses through innovative technology solutions? If working in a dynamic international company sounds like your ideal next challenge, then this opportunity is made for you!

We are currently looking for a skilled and motivated colleague to join our Professional Services Department as a Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central Consultant.

Your Responsibilities

• 
Manage and build strong relationships with our customers, acting as a trusted advisor throughout their journey

• 
Lead and contribute to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and TravelOperations implementation projects for customers across the globe

• 
Take ownership of and drive various workstreams during those implementation projects, ensuring successful delivery and customer satisfaction

• 
Provide ongoing support, consultancy, and continuous improvement recommendations to customers after Go Live, helping them maximize the value of their solutions

• 
Collaborate with our Product Department by sharing customer insights, feedback, and functional expertise to support the continued development of our solutions

Desired Skills & Requirements

Different profiles can be relevant, but the ideal candidate has the following competencies:

• 
Solid hands-on functional experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, with the ability to confidently advise customers and translate business requirements into effective solutions

• 
Experience participating in or leading Business Central/NAV implementation projects, preferably in an international environment

• 
Experience within the travel industry is an advantage but not a requirement

• 
Proactive, detail-oriented, and capable of working independently while taking ownership of your responsibilities

• 
Strong consulting, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with professional proficiency in English, both written and spoken

• 
Enjoys working in an international environment and is open to occasional travel as part of the role

What awaits you?

• 
Enjoy real influence in a fast-growing company where execution, growth, and efficiency are core values

• 
Join a leading Microsoft technology company helping global travel businesses transform and scale

• 
Be part of an international organization with colleagues across Europe, North America, Asia, and Australia

• 
Contribute to delivering innovative Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and TravelOperations solutions to travel companies worldwide, combining industry expertise with modern technology

• 
Benefit from a flexible working environment

• 
Join a strong, collaborative culture where people enjoy working together and building something meaningful

The role is based at one of our offices in Copenhagen, Aalborg, Halmstad, or Brisbane (Australia).

How to Apply

For more details, please contact, HR Manager, Nicholas Poulsen, at nop@traveloperations.com or

visit our careers site at www.traveloperations.com.

We can't wait to hear from you!

About Travel Operations A/S

At TravelOperations, we're not just about professionalism and ambition; we're about building an environment where every employee shines. Our global reach spans from Greenland to Australia, as we partner with leading travel agencies, airlines, and leisure-focused businesses to craft tailor-made solutions. Join us in reshaping the travel industry landscape, where responsiveness and innovation are our guiding stars.

Diversity and Inclusion

At our company, Diversity and Inclusion are core values. We welcome applicants of all genders, striving for a workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. Join us in building an inclusive future where diversity is celebrated as a strength.

jobs.occupation: Tjener søges til Ristorante Sole d'Italia i hjertet af København / Waiter Wanted
jobs.description:
Ristorante Sole d'Italia ligger på Gråbrødretorv midt i København. Vi laver klassisk italiensk mad fra bunden og har travlt året rundt. Vi søger nu en tjener til vores team.

Om jobbet

Du tager imod gæsterne, serverer og holder overblikket i restauranten og på terrassen. Du arbejder tæt sammen med køkkenet under service og er med til at give gæsterne en god aften.

Vi forventer

Erfaring fra restaurant eller café. At du er udadvendt og kan holde tempoet en travl aften. At du er stabil og møder til tiden. Dansk eller engelsk i det daglige.

Vi tilbyder

Et fast, erfarent team og en restaurant med travlhed året rundt. Løn efter gældende overenskomst. Arbejdstiden ligger mandag til søndag mellem kl. 06 og 04, typisk vagter 11-16 eller 16-23. Både fuldtid og deltid er muligt.

Ristorante Sole d'Italia, Gråbrødretorv 1, 1154 København K

- - -

Ristorante Sole d'Italia is located on Gråbrødretorv in central Copenhagen. We cook classic Italian food from scratch and we are busy all year round. We are looking for a waiter to join our team.

The job

You welcome the guests, serve them and keep the overview in the restaurant and on the terrace. You work closely with the kitchen during service and help give our guests a good evening.

We expect

Experience from a restaurant or cafe. That you are outgoing and can keep the pace on a busy night. That you are reliable and turn up on time. Danish or English on a daily basis.

We offer

A stable, experienced team and a restaurant that is busy all year. Salary according to the applicable collective agreement. Working hours fall Monday to Sunday between 06:00 and 04:00, typically shifts 11-16 or 16-23. Both full-time and part-time are possible.

How to apply

Send your application and CV to mail@soleditalia.dk. We interview on an ongoing basis and invite candidates for a trial shift of about three hours so we can meet in practice.

jobs.occupation: R&D Engineer – Machining
jobs.description:
DAMRC is a research and development centre for advanced manufacturing. We are internationally recognised for our work in metal processing, and our job is to turn new technology into something Danish manufacturers can use on the shop floor.

You will work both in our own R&D centre in Herning, where trials can be run without stopping a production line, and out at the companies themselves, where the solution has to survive daily use.

We are now expanding the engineering team with two R&D Engineers.

Your role

As an R&D Engineer you will work on national and international research and development projects from the first idea through to implementation, at a high international technical level. Specifically, you will:

•     Drive the development and maturation of new machining technologies in our R&D centre

•     Play a central role in process and production optimisation for industrial customers

•     Work closely with cross-functional teams and industry partners

•     Contribute to technologies that support the green transition

•     Share what you find - with engineers, production managers and machine operators alike

Who we are looking for

We are filling two positions and they do not have to be identical profiles.

Essential

•     A degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering or equivalent

•     Real understanding of machining - the process itself, not just the theory around it

•     The ability to explain a technical result clearly to very different audiences, from design engineers to machine operators

•     Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is not a requirement

Advantageous

•     Specialisation in materials engineering

•     Hands-on experience with material processing and machining techniques

•     Strong analytical skills and experience with trial design, measurement or data analysis

•     Strong IT skills and familiarity with current engineering tools and methods

Ambitious recent graduates are encouraged to apply. If you are early in your career we do not expect the experience - we expect curiosity and a willingness to get your hands dirty.

Eligibility. You must already be entitled to work in Denmark. We are not set up to handle work and residence permit applications, so we can only consider applicants who are citizens of the EU, EEA or Switzerland, or who already hold a valid Danish work permit.

What we offer

•     A high-technology research centre in strong growth, where you are invited to contribute both professionally and personally

•     Direct contact with our members and customers, and time spent inside companies most engineers never see from the inside

•     An innovative, supportive environment alongside highly skilled colleagues who share your interest in engineering

•     Work with technologies that drive the green agenda forward

Living in Herning

Interested in joining an international community in Denmark? Herning has a diverse expat network, and we will welcome you into it.

About DAMRC

DAMRC – Danish Advanced Manufacturing Research Center – is a leader in metal processing and is internationally recognised for ground-breaking innovation.

Our mission is to help Danish companies succeed through innovation and the use of the latest technology. We work in close collaboration with our members, which include several leading companies in metal processing and the machinery industry.

Since 2010 we have completed more than 400 industry projects.

We are a team of around 30 based at Industrivej Syd 17A, 7400 Herning, Denmark.

How to apply

We review applications as they arrive and will close the posting once we have found the right people, so there is no deadline — send yours when you are ready.

Send your application and CV to work@damrc.com with “R&D Engineer” in the subject line.

To hear more before applying, contact Rory Shaw (+45 2253 312/ros@damrc.com) or Sebastián Assain (+45 2222 5594/sea@damrc.com)

Your application and your personal data. We treat every application confidentially and process your personal data in accordance with the GDPR.

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor and Curator of Mammals
jobs.description:
Tenure Track Assistant Professor / Associate Professor, and Curator of Mammals at Natural History Museum Denmark
 The Natural History Museum Denmark wishes to appoint a Tenure Track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor and Curator of Mammals (mammalia) with a great vision for natural history museums in a changing world. Duties are divided equally between collection-based research and other museum duties including curation of the mammal collections, research-based teaching and supervision of students, public engagement work, and to act as the museum's liaison with relevant Danish natural history communities. The successful applicant will be expected to establish and develop an externally funded collection-based research programme/group and publish in influential journals. We particularly encourage applications from applicants with a collection-based research specialization on mammalogy. The successful applicant will be expected to curate the museum’s historically important mammal collections (56.000 specimens) requiring a thorough understanding and practical knowledge of mammal classification. We value collaboration across disciplines and professions. All applicants are expected to demonstrate interdisciplinary thinking and a commitment to working together to create solutions to global challenges. This also goes for collection work. Curators develop the collections that they are responsible for through research, field work, loan activities, digitization, acting as scientific host for visiting researchers, and increasing accessibility for everyone. This curatorial position in Mammalogy at the Natural History Museum Denmark will be filled at either the Tenure Track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor level. All curators at the Natural History Museum Denmark are expected to take a leading role in society as advocates for science and nature, creating impact at all levels while actively promoting the museum’s Vision and Values (https://snm.dk/en/about-museum). Further details of qualifications required for appointment at the museum are detailed below.

  The position is available starting March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Qualifications
 Tenure-track assistant professor
 Applicants at the tenure track assistant professor level are expected to have an academic record demonstrating the potential to deliver high profile internationally competitive research in the area of specialization. They should be a scientific specialist in one of the collection areas of the museum and have experience with collection-based research. Previous experience curating natural history collections and university teaching experience would be advantageous but is not a requirement at the time of hiring for tenure-track assistant professors. Documented interest in and experience with public engagement and community-based activities is expected. Relevant experience from a natural history museum or similar institution is an advantage.

  Associate professor
 Applicants at the associate professor level are expected to have a strong publication record in high-level, international, peer-reviewed venues in the area of specialization and a track record of successful external research funding. They should be a scientific specialist in one of the collection areas of the museum and have significant experience with collection-based research. Relevant experience from a natural history museum or similar is expected. Curatorial expertise and considerable previous experience and impact with curating and developing natural history collections is required at associate professor level. Broad experience and a compelling vision for public engagement and community-based activities is essential. Candidates are also required to have documented university-level competencies in delivering high-quality undergraduate/graduate teaching and must be able to explain and reflect upon their own teaching practice and portfolio. Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen teacher training programme for assistant professors is required.

  Assessment of applicants 
 Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research as well as their curatorial experience and potential to curate one or more of the museum’s collections. Teaching and public engagement qualifications and experience will be considered according to career level. The overall fit for the Natural History Museum will also be considered.
 Ideal applicants will have the following qualifications:

   	
• An outstanding reputation for high-quality research within Mammalogy 	
• A record of scientific use of museum collections and/or data 	
• A proven track record of interdisciplinary research 	
• Scientific expertise that ensures ability to curate Mammalia collections held by the museum 	
• Curatorial experience improving and developing natural history collections 	
• Experience from a natural history museum or similar 	
• Participation in national and international museum collaborations through organizations and programs. 	
• A vision for how digital, genomic, and other new technologies will drive advances in natural history science 	
• Ability to work at a strategic level 	
• A track record of public engagement and creating impact beyond academia 	
• Experience working on museum exhibitions, interpretation, and/or public engagement 	
• Experience in fundraising and ability to attract research funding from external sources for research, digitization and collection development. 	
• Supportive and collaborative people skills and commitment to an inclusive workplace that celebrates diversity and respect for everyone with equality and opportunity for all 	
• A passion for the vision and values of the Natural History Museum Denmark 	
• Excellent written and oral communication skills 	
• Confidence in ability to provide advocacy for the museum with multiple stakeholders   University of Copenhagen’s criteria for recognising merit
 General criteria apply to the appointment of assistant professor/associate professor at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.
 For tenure-track assistant professors
 For associate professors
 
 Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  Information on the tenure-track programme
 The tenure-track programme is a career programme and an assigned mentor will provide the tenure-track assistant professors with guidance related to career development, other academic topics and administrative procedures. Performance of the tenure-track assistant professor will be followed via internal yearly evaluations and a mid-term and final international evaluation by an assessment committee. If the ‘final appraisal’ is positive you will be promoted as associate professor. Performance and progression towards the criteria below will be evaluated with due consideration of differences between research fields. After a 6-year tenure-track period, tenure-track assistant professors are expected to meet the criteria for appointment of associate professors at the University of Copenhagen.

  About the Natural History Museum Denmark
 The Natural History Museum Denmark is the Danish national museum for nature. We work to empower citizens to connect with nature with the aim to create positive change for people and planet. We want to inspire, engage, and enable people to enjoy, understand, and care for the diversity of the natural world. The impact of climate change and anthropogenic forces on biodiversity has reached a critical point. We firmly believe that natural history museums can and should play a key role towards a more sustainable relationship with nature. We are opening a new Danish national museum for nature in spring 2027. One big museum site, in the Botanical Garden, in the centre of Copenhagen, will host state-of-the-art laboratories, outstanding research collections, new public galleries, and combined facilities for programming, education, and citizen science. It is an ambition for the museum to enhance natural history and inspire curiosity, knowledge, and empowerment for the future. The Botanical Garden was founded in 1600, and the museum’s collections date back to Ole Worm’s Cabinet of Curiosities from around 1620. With 14 million preserved specimens and living plants of 8,000 different species in the Botanical Garden, it is the largest museum collection in Denmark. It covers our planetary history with botanical, zoological, and geological specimens from all over the world. Read more about the Mammalia collection here.

  The Natural History Museum Denmark is part of the University of Copenhagen, which was founded in 1479 and is the largest university in Denmark. Read more about the museum here.
 Inquiries about the position can be made to Museum Director Nina Rønsted (e-mail: nronsted@snm.ku.dk). 

  Affirmative action
 The Natural History Museum Denmark is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, or disabled status. We are actively promoting a strategy to improve the gender balance among scientific staff. Copenhagen is a highly diverse and international Scandinavian capital with a green profile. Education is free and childcare is subsidized. Public transport is well developed, and most Copenhageners take their bike to work. There are lots of green areas in and around Copenhagen, the water in the harbor is clean enough for swimming, and the city has multiple museums and other cultural venues.

  Terms of employment
 Employment is as tenure-track assistant professor/associate professor according to the collective agreement or job structure under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The successful applicant is expected to take Danish lessons if there is no prior knowledge of Danish language. The International Office at the University of Copenhagen can help.
 This position comes with an opportunity to negotiate a start package for up to 2,500,000 DKK that will help leverage the candidate’s scientific deliverables in the initial years of employment. The negotiation for the start package takes place as part of the recruitment process. Please read about the contents of the programme and conditions, as well as UCPHs extensive support for international researchers here

  How to apply
 The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW.

  Applying for the tenure-track assistant professorship please include 

   	
• A cover letter stating the motivation for applying (1 page) 	
• Research profile: description of previous, current and future research plans (3 pages) 	
• Curatorial area, experience, vision, and interests (1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae documenting: 	 		
• Previous positions at museums, universities, or other research or cultural institutions 		
• Fundraising experience 		
• International network and relations 		
• Curatorial experience (curation of collections) 		
• Public engagement activities, i.e. citizen science projects, exhibitions, popular lectures or other relevant activities 	 	 	
• If available, description and documentation of teaching and supervision experience and qualifications- please describe and document: 	 		
• Experience with supervision of BSc- and MSc-students 		
• Teaching experience 		
• Formal pedagogical training 	 	 	
• Diplomas (MSc and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of up to 5 particularly relevant papers   Applying for the associate professorship please include 

   	
• A cover letter stating the motivation for applying (1 page) 	
• Research profile: description of previous, current and future research plans (3 pages) 	
• Curatorial area, experience, impact, vision, and interests (1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Description and documentation of teaching experience and qualifications according to university guidelines 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 5 particularly relevant papers   The deadline for applications is November 2 2026 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. We work thoroughly with this process. Several professionals from different fields must be involved. Therefore, we will not be ready for interviews until February 2027.

  You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Please refer to the following no. in future communication: 211-0260/26-2N, Tenure-track Assistant Professor and Curator of Mammals/211-0765/26-2E Associate Professor and Curator of Mammals
